Graskoue Trappers

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
Riel dancing is one of the oldest forms of dancing - thought to have evolved from
the Koi, Nama and San who used to dance in sand in a circle around a fire.

Farm workers in area have adapted it and it involves very intricate and fast dance steps.
“Dans laat die stof so staan” seems like it may have found it’s origin here. But today
there is a renewed interest in the cultural heritage of the decedents of the Khoi and San and
the art form is alive and well again.

Floris Smith who works as a chef in the Wupperthal area in the Cederberg area had a background
in classical dancing and found this art form interesting.He started coaching a local group called the "Graskoue Trappers”
and within a short time they won the ATKV Junior Riel Dance Champions.

They were then invited to compete in the World Championships of Performing Arts in California this year.

They have just arrived back in SA and a slew of medals including gold in the ethnic folk dance category.

There is also a new form of dance genre that they have developed, which is a combination of tap and Riel and they also achieved gold in this category at the World Championships. We will speak to one of the tap dancers Zarion, who says he learnt tap from his grandmother who passed it onto his mother.

Above the BUshman's kloof Lodge is San rock art and they depict dancers in a circle, we will film there and also go a bit into the history of the San.

Rags to riches story, great visuals, lovely texture.

Press Release:


Riel Dance Revival
They’re back from the World Championships of Performing Arts in California and they’ve brought home gold. How have the Nuwe Graskoue Trappers managed their remarkable revival of the Riel - one of the oldest forms of dance in South Africa? Carte Blanche meets the humble shepherds from the Cederberg who dance ‘laat die stof so staan’ and set the world of arts and culture alight.


Script:


Riel Dans Script

V/O
Boltvin Tamboer is a shepherd in a remote region of the Cederberg in the Western Cape. He is 19 years old and had to leave school, because his parents simply could not afford it any longer.
Protecting the sheep in the mountains is a solitary life and for many hours a day the only distraction he experiences is the intermittent clinking of the sheep’s bells.

Link
“But less than a month ago he was the toast of Hollywood.”

Boltvin
“Ek was 6 jaar toe ek begin het met my ouma en oupa hulle , my ma en pa hulle en so het ek groot geword met die riel.”

V/O
Boltvin is a member of the Nuwe Graskoue Trappers, a group of youngsters whose fast and intricate footwork literally left their competition in Los Angeles eating their dust.
The little sand storms made from the red velskoens form part of a uniquely South African dance that is enjoying a revival in the Western Cape.

V/O
Bertie Zass is the piano accordian player in band that accompanies the dancers.

Bertie
“Die Riel dans kom uit a lang pad dit is een van die oudste danse in Suid afrika, onder die Khoi en San gemeenskappe, en die tiepe dans was gedoen by feeste wat gehou was en gesien wat elke persoon wat by die dans passies doen het n manier wat die story vertel.

V/O
Integral to the riel, which may have been named after the Scottish Reel Dance, is that you have to dance “laat die stof so staan” or in other words in a cloud of dust.

V/O
Floris Smith is a chef at Bushman’s Kloof Lodge in the Cederberg and has a background in classical ballet . Quite by chance one weekend in 2010 his friends invited him to a Riel festival.

Bongani
“What were your impressions of Riel dans the first time?”




Floris

“I just saw men’s feet moving very fast and ladies doing imitations of house tasks and men doing imitations of animals and I did not quite understand it.”

V/O
From the hunter gatherer origins, it evolved into a courting dance in the 20th century. If a man is interested in a girl, he throws his hat in front of her and if she picks it up, a courtship could ensue. Women imitate house tasks like sweeping and cooking, while men will mimic animals to impress the women they favour.

V/O
Floris’ has always been interested in original dance forms and was captivated by the dance and he started researching Riel in his area. He found that there used to be a riel dance group that had been disbanded.

Floris
“I started asking around and meeting people in the community, there was still a handful of kids that used to be part of the original group and did a bit of dancing within the project and I started with them and it grew and got bigger.”

Little bit of upsound.

V/O

The ATKV or the Afrikaanse Taal and Kultuureverenging is an organisation that promotes Afrikaans Language and Culture. Elias Nel is the Riel Dance Project Leader is responsible for encouraging the revival in this art form. Every year groups compete against each other in the ATKV Riel Dance Championships for this sought after award.

Elias
Die riel dans wat ons vandag beoefen kan direk herlei word na die danse wat die koi en san mense vroer jare gedans het . In vandag se danse word daar nog steed in a sirkel gedans en ons moedig dit ook aan en dit herrinder net weer waar ons hierie dans gekry het. Die voorlooper van die riel dans is gewoonlik by feeste suksesvolle jagtogte of een of ander viering.

The riel dance that is practised today can be directly linked to the dances that the Khoi and San people used to dance in earlier times. That is why you will still find that it is still danced in a circle and we encourage this because it reminds us where this dance originated from.

Zarion
“Vir my as n jeugdiger is dit baie belangrik om vir my voor ouers n voorbeeld te wees om die dans weer herlewing te laat lyk . Ook om dit bekent te stel aan ander jeugdigers om te se wat hulle voor vaders se kultuur en dans gewees het.”

V/O
Graskoue Trappers ,Zarion Samson and Jobri Swart live in the little village of Suurrug.

Bongani
“I notice a lot of people when they dance they imitate an animal, what your animal?”

Zarion
“Die Bobbejaan”

Bongani
“Can you show me?”

Boys show him

V/O
Like the boys, the Khoi and San used to imitate animals that they hunted. Their influence on the area is still evident in mountains here.

Bongani Link

“The San rock art of Southern Africa is the oldest continuous rock art tradition in the world. It stretches back 20 000 years and the Bushman’s Kloof area alone there’s 137 sites.”

V/O
Environmentalist Gerhard Thom is a field guide at Bushman’s Kloof.

Bongani
“What happened to the San?”

Gerhard
“Unfortunately with colonialism and farming up of this area a lot of the hunter gatherers were forced to work on the farms, they were persecuted, a lot of them were captured and imprisoned because of live stock theft, also diseases that were brought in by the westerners decimated their populations.”

V/O
The Khoisan were highly attuned to nature and while there may not be here any longer their decendents still have that intimate rapport.

Gerhard
“The people from the Karoo and Cederberg still have that connection to the land and the Riel is just the way the dance has now changed depicting everyday life but also keeping society together.”




V/O
With the main town more than an hour away , these villages in the mountains are exceptionally isolated. There are few opportunities for the youth here, Charne Jansen is one of the dancers in the troupe.

Charne
“Die meeste jong mense is besig met verkeerde dinge. In my vrye tyd ek doen die riel dans wat my besig hou , om iets meer produktiefs te doen met my vrye tyd om met die wereldse dinge besig te hou.”

V/O
There are no formal dance classes here, the riel is learnt from birth.

Bongani
“How difficult is it to do the riel dance?”

Jobri
“Die Riel dans is baie hard om te leer. Want riel dans moet in jou gene wees. Dit is nie sommer for enige een om riel dans te dans nie.”

V/O
Floris’ intiative has gone from strength to strength in the 6 years that he has been involved with Riel. He now has 7 groups that he choreographs and manages, including these little ones called the “Boesman’skloof Stof Skoppertjies”.

Six months ago, fascinated by the nimble footwork of the Riel dance Floris tried something new.

Floris
“In December last year I had a thought, I wonder what riel would sound like in tap shoes. Cause on a rainy day we normally practice inside a hall and I started picking up on the rhythm of the riel.”

V/O
It worked so well that it developed into a new dance genre called “Riel Tap”.

Floris
“In the community themselves, when the saw the boys dancing in these shoes they started laughing and they asked me “Waar kom jy aan hierdie kap skoentjies?”
Today they cant believe what they have achieved with these kap skoentjie as they call it. “






V/O

But more success was to follow, last year the Graskoue Trappers won the national ATKV competition and then were offered a chance to represent the South Africa in the World Championships of Performing Arts in Los Angeles.

Going to Los Angeles was the stuff that dreams are made of and Floris was determined to make this dream of theirs a reality and pursued every avenue he could to get sponsorship for his dancers.

He also entered the new Riel Tap into the competition.

Floris
“They got to America, the tap category they won gold and up till today they have been dancing in tap shoes for 5 months.”

Up Sound
“Our first dance group of the night in the senior division, here are the Nuwe Grasskoue Trappers.”

V/O
With their debit on an international stage, the dancers stole the show and won gold for their performance. The band was also awarded silver medals in the music category

Zarion
“Toe ons gehoor het ons het gewen ons het trane van blydskap gestort en ons was baie opgewonde. Al ons harde werk was nie verniet nie.”

Charne
“Die kompetisie was tough, maar ons het daardeur gekom, ons was baie trots toe ons goud wen want dit is goud.”

V/O
On top of the gold medals, Boltvin, Jobri and Zarion were also awarded dance scholarships. Which means that the shepherd of the Cederberg will be soon be tapping on the timbers in Los Angeles.

Boltvin
“Ek voel baie goed daaroor, want ek het toe n kampion geword.”

Bongani
“How do you feel that Riel has taken you to all of these places?”

Jobri
“Ek het dit nooit geweet dat die riel dans sukke baie deure sal oopmaak voorentoe nie. Want ek het gedink dit sal net hier op n stil stand dood gaan. En ek was verkeerd, dit het my in 2015 in Los Angeles gebring en ek hoop dit gaan nog baie opp maak voorentoe

Floris
It is mindblowing, its really changed them as children, they have bigger dreams, aspirations to become better at what they do.”

Charne
“My grootste droom is to become a doctor one day.”

Floris
“You can dream, hope is a good thing and that is the message that they sent out to riel dancers in the project and to the bigger community as a whole.

Promo 1 - 10 seconds
V/O
Just back from Hollywood and kicking up the dust, the Nuwe Graskoue Trappers of the Cederberg are world champions of the Riel Dance.

Promo 2 - 15 seconds
V/O
With a background in classical ballet, Floris Smith has taken these dancers from the Cederberg in the Western Cape to the stages of Los Angeles, where they were crowned champions.

Promo 3 - 15 seconds
Boltvin is a humble shepherd in the Cederberg. But he is also a member of the Nuwe Graskouer Trappers, a riel dance group that won gold at the World Performing Arts Championships in Los Angeles recently.
